# TUNING — Assignment 6

All strips are **fixture captures**. Each is a preview scene rendered by Movie Maker at 30 fps, with a fixed seed set on the preview's own instance only. Setup: Godot 4.7.2, Forward+, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Laptop GPU, 1280 × 720.

Each revision below records five things:
- what I saw in the running game;
- Claude's reading of the strip before the change;
- the change itself, which I approved;
- Claude's prediction for the new strip, and its comparison of the new strip with that prediction;
- my verdict in the running game.

## 2026-11-06 — Effect A, r0 (first strip, before any tuning)

**Strip:** `captures/cover_hit_burst/r0/` — frames 10, 12, 15, 20, 30, 50 (fixture).

**Capture log:** `logs/capture_cover_hit_burst_r0.log`. It shows the device NVIDIA RTX 3060 Laptop, and one burst at frame 10 at (600.7, 349.15), rotation −π (pointing back out of the left face).

**My first look** (preview window, 1280 × 720, before any Claude read the strip), in my own words:

> 闪光看得见，正好。砖块主要往左侧飞，也不错。看得清，大小合适。大概一两秒没有了。

(English: The flash is visible and about right. The chips fly mainly to the left, which is good. It is readable and the size is right. It is gone after about one or two seconds.)

**My second look** (preview window, after viewing my own strip, before any Claude reading):

> 看得清。

(English: The chips are readable against the ground.)

Checked against the strip: the burst is gone by frame 50 (1.33 s) and only faint dust is left at frame 30 (0.67 s), so my "one or two seconds" overestimated the duration (brief R2.4).

**In the running game** (main scene, 1280 × 720, NVIDIA RTX 3060, 2026-11-06; Effect A wired in at d2d50fc). I played for a few minutes and shot at cover.

- **Four hits on one wall until it broke** — checked. Every hit was visible.
- **Firing while moving** — checked. The chips read against the ground.
- **Chips go back toward the shooter** — not checked separately.
- **Pause right after a hit** — not checked here (to be checke ...[truncated in excerpt: 2378 chars total]

2	## Frame-strip fixture for Effect A (CHANGE-BRIEF.md, Effect A "The frame strip"). Preview only:
3	## changes no game script. One real cover block (scripts/cover.gd, world = null, never hit) on the
4	## real ground tile, camera at (640, 360), zoom 1. The burst sits where a shell flying right
5	## (dir (1, 0)) touches the block's left face, drawn at shell.gd's DRAW_OFFSET, rotated to
6	## (-dir).angle() = PI, as main.gd's spawn_cover_burst() will place it.
7	## Frame numbers are Engine.get_frames_drawn(), which equals the Movie Maker frame number.
8	
9	const BURST := preload("res://effects/cover_hit_burst.tscn")
10	const COVER_HALF_WIDTH := 36.3  # cover.gd: RectangleShape2D 72.6 x 22
11	const SHELL_RADIUS := 3.0  # shell.gd: CircleShape2D radius
12	const DRAW_OFFSET := Vector2(0.0, -10.85)  # shell.gd line 5
13	const SHELL_DIR := Vector2(1, 0)
14	const FIRST_FRAME := 10
15	const RETRIGGER_FRAME := 16
16	
17	## Second burst at frame 16 (0.2 s later, inside one lifetime), for the overlap read.

19	## Fixed seed for this preview's instances only; the effect scene never sets one.
20	@export var fixed_seed := 7
21	
22	@onready var cover: Node2D = $Cover

25	var _fired := {}

27	
28	func _process(_delta: float) -> void:
29		var f := Engine.get_frames_drawn()

33		if retrigger and f >= RETRIGGER_FRAME and not _fired.has(RETRIGGER_FRAME):

content.text:
I read all six r0 frames at full size (1280 × 720). I tried to crop and enlarge them with a short Python script, but that needed approval in this session, so I didn't measure any pixels. Every position, size and colour below is my estimate by eye from the full frames. The burst sits at (600.7, 349.15), on the left end of the cover block, rotated −π, so the chips fly left over the open ground.

## What each frame shows

| Frame | Time | What I see |
|---|---|---|
| **10** | 0 s | A bright cream-white disc about 45 px across, centred on the block's left end and spilling over the brick. Its edge looks almost hard. **No chips are visible**: they are still inside the 4 px emission sphere, pale #E8D8B0 on a near-white flash. There is no dust yet. |
| **12** | 0.07 s | The flash is still near full brightness and about the same size. A thin crescent of small pale peach chips sits on its left edge, only about 10–20 px out. No dust is separate from the flash yet. |
| **15** | 0.17 s | The flash is gone. A pale sand dust puff about 25–30 px across sits on the block's left end. About 20 chips, now orange-red, sit in a wide arc 25–50 px left of the impact point, spread about ±40 px up and down. This is the best frame for the chips: they read clearly against the dark ground. |
| **20** | 0.33 s | The dust is now the main element: about 45–50 px across, pale, partly over the brick. **The chips have almost disappeared.** I can find only a few faint dark-red specks around x ≈ 545–575. |
| **30** | 0.67 s | A very faint grey haze to the upper left of the block. No chips. |
| **50** | 1.33 s | Nothing left; the block is clean. |

## Comparison with the intent block

1. **Timing, dissipation phase (chips).** The brief's frame-20 row says "chips almost stopped, about 2 hull widths out, red-brown and smaller". In r0 the chips are nearly invisible by frame 20, so they read on screen only from about frame 12 to frame 17 (0.2 s).
